source.title: Revisiting Model Stitching In the Foundation Model Era
source.authors: Zheda Mai; Kexin Zhang; Fu-En Wang; Zixiao Wang; Albert Y. C. Chen; Lu Xia; Min Sun; Wei-Lun Chao; Cheng-Hao Kuo

record.tranche_reason: Tests representational compatibility using learned model stitching and downstream accuracy, rather than the original sources’ similarity measurements.
record.gate_note: The study measures learned stitching outcomes and reports accuracy and feature-distance results. Table 1 reports stitch-position and training-strategy results; its rows are included below. Table 2 and supplementary Table 7 provide selected cross-task and cross-model outcomes. The paper also reports feature distances in Figure 2, but only as plots without extractable numerical values; they are not separate rows. Numbers from cited studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains only a light stitch layer (MLP, linear or LoRA) between frozen, independently trained VFMs (DINOv2, SigLIP2, CLIP, DINOv3). It measures downstream accuracy or mIoU against target linear probes and self-stitch controls. This directly tests whether one model's representations can be mapped onto another's with little loss (V4), using functional stitching rather than similarity metrics. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that heterogeneous VFMs are reliably stitchable when the stitch layer is trained with final feature matching then task fine-tuning. They find naive LFM and task-loss training fail, especially at shallow positions. Stitched models often beat self-stitch controls, which the authors read as fusion of complementary knowledge. They also report that task-agnostic stitch training suggests a fundamental alignment between the representation spaces, and propose the VFM Stitch Tree.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned stitch layers and downstream task accuracy to assess functional compatibility, rather than measuring general representational similarity or convergence as models scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Stitch training strategy (no pretraining, LFM, or FFM), stitch position, stitch-layer family, source/target choice, dataset, and task affect results. FFM helps particularly at shallow positions; CLIP as source is reported as an exception in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-VFM stitched models outperform both self-stitch controls and fall into rescue/preserve cases more than interference cases. The authors read this as fusion of complementary knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heterogeneous VFMs hold complementary information that stitching can combine beyond either model alone.

record.problems: Stitching accuracy is a functional compatibility proxy, not a direct test of convergence in pairwise input distances. The reported representation-distance comparison is figure-only without numerical values in the text. The study does not vary model scale or capability, and gives no uncertainty estimates. The task-specific evaluation centers on a limited set of VFM families and datasets.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted Table 2 fMoW results that overlap the Table 1 fMoW results; other iNaturalist stitch positions in Table 2; most CLIP/DINOv3 pairings in Supplementary Tables 7–11; and the full tables for alternative stitch-layer families and multimodal VST evaluations. The paper reports these in Table 2, Table 3, Supplementary Tables 7–11, and Tables 5, 13–14. Figure-only feature-distance values were not extracted because the text provides no numeric values.

untested.parts: No image–caption paired alignment as vision and language models improve. Only vision towers are stitched.
Relative representations, mapping without paired data, and stitching outside vision encoders are not tested. Linear maps are tested only in Table 3 (declared as left out).
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits.
No alternative similarity metrics, neighbour settings or OOD inputs. Dependence on the stitch-training objective is captured under V4 instead.
No test of plateau or of shared data/objectives as the cause of alignment.

missing.what: Frozen stitch results with no task fine-tuning, measured by linear probe. LFM S→D gives 29.9–47.2 and D→S 45.3–51.0; FFM S→D gives 43.3–50.8 and D→S 51.0–56.1. Targets are DINOv2 46.7 and SigLIP2 53.5. This is the closest test of little-loss mapping.
FGVC-Aircraft stitched vs self-stitch results at layers 6/14/22: D→S 77.8/87.6/92.4 and S→D 80.7/89.0/91.0, against D self 37.8/79.3/91.2 and S self 67.9/88.1/89.3.

record.verdict_notes: V7 links were removed: shallow and CLIP shortfalls reflect training method or a weak source encoder, not convergence limits or shared-data causes. Rows R49–R52 need their condition fixed to task-agnostic. Table 1 baselines are lenient because the stitch includes task tuning. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep; it does not test whether alignment rises as independently trained models become larger or more capable.
Includes vision-language models but does not measure image-caption representation alignment as both models improve.
Does not compare training seeds or shared features/subspaces across seeds of the same architecture.

Tests learned stitch layers on paired inputs and downstream task performance. Does not test relative representations, stitching layers together, or alignment without paired inputs. Accuracy compatibility does not establish that representations map with little loss under all measures.
Does not identify recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Compares stitch-training objectives, but does not test robustness across alternative representation-similarity measures, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports conditions where stitching is incomplete or fails to match a reference, but does not test whether a plateau occurs or whether shared data/objectives cause the observed compatibility.
